explanation: OEIS A331631 (repeatedly take the least missing S and adjoin S, 3S, 9S, … through the first positive power whose value contains S as a decimal substring): 'This is conjectured to be a permutation of the positive integers.' FollowsRule encodes this exactly: each block starts at the least missing positive value, StopsAt picks the first positive exponent with S an infix of S·3^j, the block includes that term (as in the DATA, e.g. 81 ends the first block), and blocks are consecutive. The statement asserts a rule-following sequence that is injective and surjective onto the positive integers. If some block never stopped, no rule-following sequence would exist and the conjecture would also fail, so the existential form is equivalent. Faithful.
